_comment: Project registry for the website, gallery and Dalamud installer. kind separates plugins, companion tools and bundled libraries. Source visibility does not imply a release. released indicates a stable installer fallback; testingVersion indicates a published testing artifact.

mods.name: Ghostty
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Eorzea is a terminal multiplexer.
mods.description: Quake-style dropdown, floating windows and terminals pinned in the world, connected to shells on your own machine through ghostty-agent. /term to toggle. Works with or without Umbra; with Umbra, the Ghostty toolbar widget shows its status and a popup terminal.
mods.needs: ghostty-agent running on the machine the game runs on.
mods.status: released · experimental preview
mods.verification: Selected ground-placement and world-panel behavior was observed in earlier builds. The latest release changes, controller behavior and full window lifecycle still require live acceptance. Host tests do not certify every platform.

mods.name: Almanac
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Talk to a local AI model in game, with XivMcp's tools.
mods.description: Connects a model running on your own PC (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or any OpenAI-compatible server) to the game through XivMcp. Setup wizard with GPU-aware model recommendations, an in-game chat with threads and streaming, and a benchmark you can share with the community leaderboard. No cloud, no Python. Requires the XivMcp plugin for game tools.
mods.needs: A local model server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or any OpenAI-compatible API), and XivMcp for game tools.
mods.status: stable and testing builds · live coverage remains limited
mods.verification: Core model, MCP, thread and benchmark logic has host-side tests. In-game UI, GPU detection, live model/tool calls and benchmark output still require acceptance.

mods.name: XivMcp
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Model Context Protocol server for FINAL FANTASY XIV.

mods.status: released · selected in-game calls verified
mods.verification: Selected game-state calls were observed in earlier builds. The latest testing package has offline validation; loading it, approvals and current HUD-family integration still require live acceptance.

mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Launch Linux desktop apps into the game world.

mods.name: XivArcade
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Your own classic games as game panels, with saves kept in step across your machines.
mods.description: A library for the classic games you own, for FINAL FANTASY XIV running under Wine on Linux. /arcade lists the game files in folders you choose, starts them in RetroArch on the Linux host, and shows them as world panels through Ghostty when it is installed. Every save and save state lives in one folder that Syncthing copies between your machines. It downloads no games, BIOS files or artwork.

mods.name: XivWayfinder
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: A softly glowing bead and the classic pointing glove show which way to go.
mods.description: XivWayfinder points the way in FINAL FANTASY XIV: a softly pulsing bead floats a couple of yalms ahead of you in the direction to go, and the game's own white pointing glove points there too, sliding to the edge of the screen when the way is behind you. It follows, in order, a target you set with /wayfinder X Y or another plugin sets over IPC, your map flag, and your tracked quest's next step; in another zone it names the nearest aetheryte instead. With vnavmesh installed it points along the walkable path. It only points and never moves your character.
mods.needs: Nothing beyond Dalamud (API 15), on Windows or Linux under Wine. vnavmesh is optional, for walkable paths.
mods.build: tools/fetch-dalamud.sh, then tools/install-dev.sh (or dotnet build XivWayfinder.slnx -c Release)
mods.status: released · newer guide work remains experimental
mods.verification: The latest testing build passes offline logic, model-pack, shader-checksum and packaging checks. Live rendering, collision, boarding, teleport, controller behavior and navigation handoffs still require acceptance.

mods.name: XivLantern
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Light a lantern for your friends: a friend list, 1:1 chat and channels of your own, peer to peer.
mods.description: Friends light a lantern to say they are here. Add friends with a one-time invite, see whose lantern is lit, chat 1:1 and in channels you make, and hear from the mod's author in a channel only they can post to. Peer to peer over iroh: no Lantern server, and nothing from the game is ever sent — not your character's name, world or chat; your friends see the name you type. Off until you turn it on in settings, where it says exactly who can see what (including that relays see your IP address, and how to turn them off). Blocking, rate limits and no auto-accept.
mods.needs: Nothing beyond Dalamud (API 15); the network layer ships inside the plugin as lantern.dll. Friends running XivLantern too.
mods.build: tools/build-native.sh (cargo and mingw-w64), then dotnet build src/XivLantern.Plugin/XivLantern.Plugin.csproj -c Release and tools/package.sh
mods.status: released · newer communication work remains experimental
mods.verification: The latest testing build passes native default/optional-feature tests, C# binding tests, core tests and packaging checks. Windows/Wine execution, in-game UI and communication extensions still require acceptance for this build.

mods.name: XivPiano
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Your Pandora stations inside FFXIV: play, skip, thumbs, new stations.
mods.description: XivPiano is a Pandora radio player inside FINAL FANTASY XIV, in the tradition of pianobar and Pithos. Sign in with your Pandora account and play your stations, skip, thumbs up or down, shelve a song you are tired of, bookmark it, ask why it was picked, and make new stations from an artist, a song or a genre. The song shows in the server info bar; /piano next and friends work from chat and macros, and other plugins can control it over IPC. It can mute the game's music while it plays and pause itself during cutscenes. Pandora is only available in the United States. Not affiliated with Pandora or Sirius XM. Optional Spaceghost Scrobbles keeps a private listening history, with export, deletion and user-controlled forwarding to ListenBrainz or Last.fm. Your Pandora account and stream URLs are never sent to the scrobbling service.
mods.needs: Dalamud (API 15), on Windows or Linux under Wine, and a Pandora account in the United States.
mods.build: tools/fetch-dalamud.sh, then tools/install-dev.sh (or dotnet build XivPiano.slnx -c Release)
mods.status: stable release available · native melodica protocol · private scrobbling
mods.verification: Native melodica protocol, private listening history and optional ListenBrainz/Last.fm forwarding are implemented. Live Pandora authentication, audible playback, in-game transitions still require player acceptance.

sections.title: One illustrated Umbra family
sections.body: Journal, Character, Vitals, Combat, Correspondence, Inventory, Crafting and Floating Windows form one interface family. Explore every module, toolbar adapter and presentation option.

sections.title: Keep the original within reach
sections.body: Click the HUD entry in Umbra’s server-info bar or use /xivhud on. Restore chat, nameplates and action bars with /xivhud off. Your saved HUD layout is preserved, and unloading releases the visibility change.

sections.title: Windows that fit the moment
sections.body: Screen and native frames remain available. XivHud.Windows provides independent floating presentation for open plugin windows without a Ghostty session. Journal and Character choose this service by default for world mode; their appearance settings can explicitly select the existing Ghostty host. Recover all standalone windows with /xivwindows screen.

sections.title: Your assistant can see the interface
sections.body: The new XivMcp integration reads every module’s readiness, current window mode and selection. Explicit UI changes wait for your approval. It can open a chapter, select a Character page or restore a screen window without simulating controller input.

sections.title: What has been checked
sections.body: The nine modules and eight Umbra adapters loaded in game. Recorded checks cover standalone Journal placement and its settings popup, Inventory selection, beside-character projection, screen recovery, and Crafting worklist totals. All 548 offline tests pass. Physical controller navigation and scene depth occlusion remain unverified.

mods.verification: HUD restoration was observed in earlier builds. HUD, Journal and Character modules loaded and exposed read-only IPC snapshots in the recorded checks. UI mutations, visual transitions and physical controller navigation still require acceptance.

sections.title: A woven map underfoot
sections.body: A connected cloth rug carries the current game map beneath your character. Choose a circular mat or rounded rectangle, adjust map coverage and cloth appearance, and show Wayfinder’s route when it is installed.

sections.title: Music in the weave
sections.body: With XivPiano, played audio can ripple through the cloth or drive ten optional 3-D visualizations. Reduced-motion settings stop musical motion, and missing or stale audio makes the visuals quiet. Rug does not require Piano or Ghostty.

sections.title: A prototype with measured limits
sections.body: Selected flat scenes, map imagery, foliage occlusion and native Journal overlap have been observed. Continuous terrain coverage, stairs, stacked floors, jumping, device resets and frame cost remain under development. Native composition hides the rug when its required rendering stage is unavailable.

sections.title: Controls and compatibility
sections.body: /rug opens settings. Music, cloth motion, jump catch and optional local visual poses have separate controls. XivRug does not move or teleport your character. Existing development installs may be named XivFloorMap: preserve their settings and disable that copy before loading XivRug. The source retains a compatibility build; these are one project.

sections.title: Diagnostics for your assistant
sections.body: XivMcp can discover Rug and read its renderer, terrain, composition, map and music status through the new read-only status interface. The interface does not start terrain probes or change settings.

mods.verification: Selected flat scenes and Journal overlap were observed in earlier builds. Current diagnostics have offline validation. Continuous terrain, stairs, device resets, frame cost and music visuals still require acceptance.

mods.name: XivStream

sections.title: Play on the screen you choose
sections.body: XivStream sets up your modded FFXIV host for Moonlight clients or browser streaming. Its wizard detects the machine, then asks for the choices it cannot infer.

sections.title: Review the plan
sections.body: xivstream detect describes the host, xivstream plan -v shows planned commands and file changes, and xivstream doctor checks the setup. Review the plan before applying it.

sections.title: A host tool
sections.body: This runs outside the game and is downloaded from its GitHub releases. It is not installed through Dalamud’s plugin repository. The same source project contains Sunshine, Wolf and Selkies setup options.

sections.title: What has been tested
sections.body: The recorded streaming path uses Incus, Sunshine and NVIDIA. Recent source fixes cover pending pairing requests and input-device registration; Wolf performance parity and other host/backend combinations are not established. The pairing and input fixes are merged into source but are newer than the published release candidate.

mods.verification: The recorded streaming path uses Incus, Sunshine and NVIDIA. Recent source fixes cover pending pairing requests and input-device registration; Wolf performance parity and other host/backend combinations are not established.

mods.name: XivHud Windowing
mods.punchline: Shared hosting and IPC for the HUD family.
mods.description: Shared exact-identity adoption protocol, independent floating and Ghostty adapters, native frames and versioned IPC.
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.status: developer library · bundled with consuming modules

sections.title: Bundled, independently optional providers
sections.body: AdoptedWindowHost implements provider-neutral exact-identity ownership. FloatingWindowHost talks to XivHud.Windows; GhosttyWindowHost preserves the existing Ghostty path. The router releases one provider before requesting another. Native frames share the owned draw-list capture code and remain optional.

sections.title: IPC and ownership
sections.body:
The HUD host, Journal and Character expose versioned JSON Call gates. Reads return immutable snapshots; changes are validated, queued, applied on the framework thread and polled by request ID. Controller ownership stays with a focused local window and is never offered as an MCP operation.

See the IPC contract and the module READMEs for lifecycle, window identity and build instructions.

mods.verification: Libraries are bundled with consuming HUD modules. Read-only IPC snapshots were checked; all frame/world hosting transitions and controller navigation still require acceptance.

sections.title: A second HUD, on your side of the connection
sections.body: Keep FFXIV on its game screen and place selected information in your glasses or another display. The computer running FFXIV supplies game state; the receiving device handles display detection. When playing natively, the same computer can supply game state to its local companion viewer.

sections.title: An app when you just want Prism
sections.body: The planned standalone Prism Display app receives HUD information without opening Moonlight. Phone, tablet, desktop and glasses outputs can have different layouts. A browser preview below demonstrates the layout choices with invented data.

sections.title: Native Moonlight, with Prism around the game
sections.body: Combined mode is planned for native Moonlight applications. Ordinary overlays will be evaluated where supported; restricted platforms may need a Prism-enabled native Moonlight build. Presentation support must be verified for each receiving device, operating system and connected display.

sections.title: Peripheral first, pinned afterward
sections.body: Start with sparse, readable panels and a clear centre. Whole-surface pinning can use capabilities already supplied by the glasses. Independent spatial panels and physical-monitor alignment are later work, depending on tracking and calibration.

sections.title: Remember the glasses you actually use
sections.body: Associate a display with a profile once. During an active companion session, plugging in those glasses should activate that profile. Unplugging, stale data and viewer failure must close the output and release any optional native HUD relocation.

sections.title: The HUD family, connected
sections.body: Journal, Character, Wayfinder and Piano are planned panel sources. XivMcp will report viewer readiness, actual presentation and recovery state. The display feed will be independent of high-frequency MCP tool calls.

sections.title: Compatibility is a test record
sections.body: Windows clients, Android phone and wearable clients, and iPadOS are targets. Ordinary display output, simultaneous Moonlight use, whole-surface pinning and spatial panels are separate capabilities. No glasses model, native companion app or live game connection has been verified yet.

mods.punchline: Slack, within reach.
mods.description: A practical Slack companion project for FFXIV: DMs, mentions, threads and persistent drafts, with quiet play sessions and optional Prism panels.
mods.status: design preview; live plugin and native companion apps are not released

sections.title: The conversations you actually need
sections.body: The first dedicated interface is planned around DMs, mentions and pinned channels. Read a thread, keep a draft, react or open the original message. The interactive preview uses a fictional workspace and never connects to Slack.

sections.title: A useful path before a complete custom client
sections.body: First evaluate hosting the official Slack app window through Desktop and Ghostty in the Wine/Linux setup. A dedicated compact interface then uses supported Slack APIs and workspace-authorized access. Official app hosting is planned, not verified.

sections.title: Your identity, your deliberate send
sections.body: A real client needs authorized user access, rather than silently substituting a bot identity. Credentials stay in the connector on a trusted device. Sending and reactions are explicit actions; an assistant never sends merely because a message appeared.

sections.title: Quiet while you play
sections.body: Choose when a conversation deserves attention. Compact notifications, a quiet session and drafts that survive closing the panel make a more useful first release than an attempt to reproduce every Slack feature.

sections.title: A conversation panel for Prism and Camp
sections.body: Dispatch will offer a compact panel for glasses or another display and a larger window in a Camp arrangement. Viewers receive only the conversations you choose. A controller should open or dismiss a panel without stealing ordinary game input.

sections.title: What still needs proving
sections.body: OAuth, workspace installation policy, event delivery, history limits, message identity and permission revocation need integration checks. There is no Slack connection, live account access or installable Dalamud plugin in this publication.

mods.name: XivCamp
mods.punchline: Unfold your little corner of Eorzea.
mods.description: A saved-layout project for your map rug, journal, music, conversations and world windows. Make a campfire, work corner or adventure arrangement and return to it.
mods.status: design preview; live plugin and native companion apps are not released

sections.title: A place for the tools you already have
sections.body: Campfire brings Rug, Piano, Journal and Lantern together. Work corner adds Dispatch, notes and a terminal. Adventure favours Wayfinder and compact Prism information. Each arrangement remembers what belongs there.

sections.title: Begin on the screen
sections.body: The first implementation target is a saved screen layout: panel selection, position, size and display assignment. The interactive preview switches invented arrangements and exports a draft. It does not move real plugin windows.

sections.title: Then unfold it into the world
sections.body: Ghostty world windows and Rug placement are later integrations. A scene should retain an ordinary screen recovery path whenever a world host is missing or unavailable. A picture of a campsite is concept artwork, not evidence that furniture is being spawned.

sections.title: One arrangement, several displays
sections.body: With Prism, a Camp arrangement can send navigation to glasses, a journal to a tablet and work conversations to another monitor. Display mappings remain owned by the receiving client.

sections.title: Controller-friendly and reversible
sections.body: Opening Camp should have explicit focus ownership. Closing it, switching scenes or losing an optional provider should restore the previous arrangement. Missing panels should be reported individually rather than breaking the whole scene.

sections.title: What still needs proving
sections.body: Live window ownership, restoring positions, world placement, music actions and controller navigation need acceptance with the actual modules. There is no live plugin integration or installable Dalamud release in this publication.

sections.body: Session conversations, channel chapters, explicit message composition and a notification center on warm vellum. The family uses stitched leather, brass, compass ornament and game fonts. Explore the Umbra UI family.

sections.title: Open from Umbra
sections.body: Use the optional Umbra.XivHud.Chat toolbar plugin, or /xivchat open. Right-click the toolbar button for appearance settings. Ctrl+Shift+right-click retains Umbra widget settings.

sections.title: Development installation
sections.body: The modules use the explicit development Dalamud repository. Umbra toolbar DLLs are separate assets in the same development release. Add the adapter DLL in Umbra Settings → Plugins, restart Umbra, then choose the widget in the toolbar editor.

sections.title: Keep the original within reach
sections.body: Native chat, hotbars and job gauges remain available. Preview data is labelled and cannot send chat or trigger actions. Chat history stays in memory for the current session.

mods.verification: The redesigned modules and Umbra toolbar adapters loaded live; the live capture shows the shared illustrated style beside the quest tracker. Explicit combat action correctness and actual chat delivery remain acceptance checks.

sections.title: Open the window
sections.body: Float open plugin windows beside your character, in view, in the world or on the ground. No Ghostty or virtual terminal is required. Use /xivwindows or its optional Umbra.XivHud.Windows toolbar button. Each module works without Umbra.

sections.title: Independent floating presentation
sections.body: Open /xivwindows, choose an open plugin window, then Float selected. Choose Beside me, View, Here or Ground. Screen returns one source; /xivwindows screen recovers all sources. Closing the host restores their ordinary screen rendering.

sections.title: Development installation

sections.title: Local and remote windows
sections.body:
Local plugin windows use the standalone texture host and allocate no terminal sessions. Ghostty keeps its existing terminal and remote-desktop panel behavior. This release does not export an in-game plugin window to a phone or another computer. That needs a separate authenticated stream transport; it is not implied by a local world placement.

World panels are projected overlays. Scene-depth occlusion, generic native-addon capture and physical controller acceptance are not established by these builds.
